title: Postbox’s module graph
note: A replay of a recorded real session in three of its real turns: @builder’s turn that handed the app to @critic, @critic’s first review, and @builder’s first turn that started after that review. Each says that turn’s words, shows the last version it made, and reports its recorded cost. recordedTurns lists every real turn; notReplayed names the ones the replay leaves out, and edits what it changes.
ask: @builder The server/ and app/js/ folders here are copies of Postbox’s own source. Show me its module dependency graph, computed from the files’ imports yourself and embedded in the app, as one picture of all the modules: each a node sized by how many modules import it, the clusters that belong together drawn together, the near-cycles visible, and how far a change to one module ripples through what imports it when I pick it. Let the network carry the answer, not lists.

said: I’m computing the import graph from the 451 files now (1,605 imports found, including 93 dynamic `import()` calls), then building the app.
The app is up as v1; I’m looking at it now to fix the layout before handing it off.
Ripple rings now render correctly; fixing label visibility and capping the map height, then restoring the normal start view.
The map now fits on one screen with readable labels; checking Postbox’s browser check before posting the review.
Wide view looks clean. Checking the 375 px result from Postbox’s check.
Waiting on Postbox’s check of v9; viewing it meanwhile, which also triggers the render.
I’ll inspect the app and its graph code, then pin concrete fixes to the review.

Requested changes with four pinned comments: correct the cycle claims, clarify the dynamic-import toggle’s scope, show import direction, and disclose the alternative paths hidden by ripple rings. The wide light-theme layout is readable, but these issues make the graph’s behavior and relationships misleading.

I didn’t change anything: both warnings describe versions the app has already replaced. The current version, v9, passed Postbox’s browser check.

- **First list:** its numbers come from v1, with a 747 px tall map, 8 px labels and dashes under 1 px. Versions 4–7 shortened the map to 430 px, kept labels at 13 px on screen at every width, and set dashes to 4/3 px.
- **Second list:** the 1 px dashed line was the shared-module ring in the legend, which v9 fixed.

The review block for v9 is still open for critic.
v10 is up, addressing all four review comments; checking how it renders.
Now resolving the four review threads on the block.

The app is now on version 11; it passed Postbox’s browser check, and each of critic’s four comments has a resolved reply in the review.

- **Cyclic groups:** I counted wrong before. All 11 groups of modules that reach each other need an `import()` call to close; none hold together with plain imports alone. Three of them contain a smaller loop made only of plain imports. I tested each `import()` inside a group by removing it: 22 of them split their group on their own, and those are drawn thicker.
- **The `import()` switch:** unticking it now recomputes node sizes, the groups (11 drop to 3), the headline and the menu counts.
- **Direction and ripple lines:** highlighted lines now carry arrows from importer to the module it imports. When a module is picked, you can switch between “One shortest path each” and “All links”; with All links, imports that loop back toward the picked module show in the accent color.

I looked at the map view after the change, but not at the All links view.
I didn’t change anything: the small-marks warning came from version 10. Version 11 already keeps every node at least 4 px across on narrow screens, and Postbox’s browser check passed on it.

review.fallback: Review of Postbox module dependency graph: comment in the chat.

comments.text: The headline calls 11 strongly connected components “11 import cycles” and says eight are kept apart by one dynamic import. An SCC can contain many cycles, and the code does not establish that removing one dynamic edge breaks each group. Likewise, the legend’s 44 is every dynamic edge inside an SCC, not 44 verified cycle-closing imports. Call these cyclic groups, distinguish static and dynamic-dependent groups, and only claim a single closing edge after testing its removal.

Unticking “count import() as a dependency” on the initial Map produces no visible change: filtering is conditional on R0, and cycle highlights, sizes, picker counts, and headline remain based on all edges. Either scope and label this control explicitly as “Include import() in ripple” and enable it when a module is selected, or recompute the displayed graph statistics and cyclic groups for the selected dependency set.

All import edges are undirected-looking lines, including the prominent cycle edges. The picture cannot tell the reader who imports whom or let them trace a directed loop. Add arrowheads or directional marks for selected relationships and highlighted cycles, with an explicit importer → dependency legend; keep those marks legible when zoomed out.

Ripple rings display only one BFS predecessor per reached module via onPath, hiding every alternative dependency path. This makes a densely connected dependency graph look like a tree without saying so, and hides the very feedback relationships the app is intended to reveal. Label the emphasized lines as “one shortest path per module” and provide a way to show all dependencies among reached modules, including cycle edges.
